flashcards.question: What is E-Commerce?
flashcards.answer:
E-commerce refers to the buying and selling of goods or services via the internet, including the transfer of money and data needed to complete transactions.

• Takes place online
• Involves products, services, payments, and data
• Also called electronic commerce or internet commerce
flashcards.explanation: The foundation of modern digital business.

flashcards.question: How has E-Commerce transformed the Hospitality Industry?
flashcards.answer:
Main transformation areas:

• Online platforms replaced phone/in-person bookings
• Customer interaction moved to digital channels
• Services became faster, more personalized, and global
• Hotels and travel companies now depend on digital systems
flashcards.explanation: Traditionally, hospitality relied on face-to-face interaction.

flashcards.question: What are the benefits of Online Booking Systems?
flashcards.answer:
Benefits for businesses:

• Better booking management
• Higher occupancy rates
• Reduced manual work
• Customers can reserve rooms anytime from anywhere
flashcards.explanation: Digital transformation in hospitality starts with booking systems.

flashcards.question: What is Dynamic Pricing?
flashcards.answer:
Prices change in real time depending on:

• Demand
• Seasonality
• Competitor prices

This allows businesses to maximize revenue based on market conditions.
flashcards.explanation: AI and algorithms enable real-time price optimization.

flashcards.question: How do Virtual Tours and AR enhance customer engagement?
flashcards.answer:
Customers can explore hotels digitally before booking.

Example: The Ritz-Carlton Bali offers a 360-degree virtual tour of rooms and facilities.

Benefits:
• Reduces uncertainty
• Increases booking confidence
flashcards.explanation: Virtual reality creates immersive preview experiences.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Hotel E-Commerce and General E-Commerce?
flashcards.answer:
HOTEL E-COMMERCE:
• Focus: Accommodation and hospitality
• Products: Hotel rooms, spa, restaurants
• Platforms: Agoda, Expedia

GENERAL E-COMMERCE:
• Focus: Selling goods across many industries
• Products: Electronics, clothing, groceries
• Platforms: Amazon, eBay, Walmart

Key difference: Hotel e-commerce is specialized, general is broad.
flashcards.explanation: Understanding the specialization of hotel digital commerce.

flashcards.question: What are the 4 pillars of the Digital Future of Hospitality?
flashcards.answer:
1. INNOVATION - Constant technological improvement
2. CUSTOMER FOCUS - Personalized and seamless experiences
3. GLOBAL EXPANSION - Borderless business opportunities
4. SUSTAINABILITY - Eco-conscious solutions
flashcards.explanation: The main directions for hospitality digital transformation.

flashcards.question: What is B2C (Business to Consumer)?
flashcards.answer:
B2C = Business sells directly to consumers

Examples:
• Amazon
• Walmart
• Online retail stores

flashcards.question: What is B2B (Business to Business)?
flashcards.answer:
B2B = Businesses sell to other businesses

Examples:
• Manufacturers to wholesalers
• Software providers to companies
• Wholesale platforms

flashcards.question: What is D2C (Direct to Consumer)?
flashcards.answer:
D2C = Brands sell directly to customers WITHOUT intermediaries

• No retailer or wholesaler involved
• Often supported by social media
• Brand-owned websites

Example: Nike selling directly through nike.com

flashcards.question: What is C2C (Consumer to Consumer)?
flashcards.answer:
C2C = Consumers sell to other consumers

Examples:
• eBay
• Etsy
• Facebook Marketplace
• Craigslist

flashcards.question: What is C2B (Consumer to Business)?
flashcards.answer:
C2B = Individuals offer products or services to companies

Examples:
• Influencers
• Photographers
• Freelancers
• Stock photo contributors

flashcards.question: What are B2G and C2G e-commerce models?
flashcards.answer:
B2G (Business to Government), also called B2A:
• Businesses sell goods/services to government entities
• Example: contractors cleaning and maintaining public parks

C2G (Consumer to Government), also called C2A:
• Consumers provide feedback or transact with public agencies
• Example: paying an electricity bill or taxes through a government website
flashcards.explanation: The two government-related models — completing all 7 business models from Unit 1.

flashcards.question: What are Physical Goods, Digital Goods, and Services in E-Commerce?
flashcards.answer:
PHYSICAL GOODS:
• Tangible products with physical form
• Need shipping

DIGITAL GOODS:
• Intangible products delivered electronically
• E-books, software, music

SERVICES:
• Activities that deliver value
• Consulting, design, bookings
flashcards.explanation: Three types of products sold online.

options: Reduce uncertainty and increase booking confidence

learn.title: The Context of Modern E-Commerce
learn.content:
What is E-Commerce?

E-Commerce = Buying and selling goods/services via the internet
Includes: Products + Services + Payments + Data

Digital Transformation in Hospitality

  • Online Booking: Reserve rooms anytime, anywhere
  • Personalization: Customized experiences using data
  • Dynamic Pricing: Real-time price changes
  • Virtual Tours: 360° previews before booking

E-Commerce Business Models

  • B2C: Business → Consumer (Amazon)
  • B2B: Business → Business (Wholesale)
  • C2C: Consumer → Consumer (eBay)
  • D2C: Direct to Consumer (Brand websites)
  • C2B: Consumer → Business (Freelancers)

4 Pillars of Digital Hospitality Future

🚀 Innovation - Technology improvement

👤 Customer Focus - Personalized experiences

🌍 Global Expansion - Borderless business

🌱 Sustainability - Eco-conscious solutions

flashcards.question: What is the Tourism Distribution System?
flashcards.answer:
The tourism distribution system explains how tourism products reach the customer.

It connects:
• Primary suppliers
• Intermediaries
• Digital platforms
• Final customers

E-business platforms make this process faster, global, and automated.
flashcards.explanation: The pathway from supplier to traveler.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Tour Operator and Travel Agent?
flashcards.answer:
TOUR OPERATOR:
• Creates its own tourism product
• Combines services into package trips
• Acts as organizer or wholesaler

TRAVEL AGENT:
• Does NOT create products
• Sells products created by others
• Acts only as intermediary
• Earns income through commission

flashcards.question: Who are the Primary Suppliers in tourism?
flashcards.answer:
Primary suppliers create the core tourism product:

• Accommodation providers (hotels)
• Airlines
• Transport companies
• Cruise companies
• Attractions and activities
flashcards.explanation: The original producers of tourism services.

flashcards.question: What are Wholesalers or Bedbanks?
flashcards.answer:
Wholesalers/Bedbanks:

• Buy services in bulk
• Work with net rates
• Focus on B2B relationships
• Rarely sell directly to individuals
• Platforms are often password-protected
flashcards.explanation: Bulk buyers in the tourism chain.

flashcards.question: What is a Global Distribution System (GDS)?
flashcards.answer:
A GDS is:
• A global network
• Connecting travel suppliers with travel agencies
• Enabling automated bookings

Main users:
• Airlines
• Hotels
• Car rental companies

Examples: Amadeus, Sabre, Travelport

flashcards.question: What is a Property Management System (PMS)?
flashcards.answer:
PMS or CRS (Central Reservation System):

• Internal systems used by suppliers
• Manage reservations, availability, and operations
• Do NOT sell directly to customers
• Connect to other platforms for distribution

flashcards.question: What is a Booking Engine?
flashcards.answer:
A booking engine:

• Allows online booking on the supplier's own website
• Supports direct sales
• Connects directly with PMS
• Enables real-time availability

flashcards.question: What is a Channel Manager?
flashcards.answer:
A Channel Manager:

• Manages room rates and availability
• Synchronizes ALL sales channels in real time
• Reduces overbooking risk
• Modern versions often use AI
flashcards.explanation: Keeps all booking channels in sync.

flashcards.question: What are Meta-Search Engines?
flashcards.answer:
Meta-search engines:

• Compare offers from multiple OTAs and supplier websites
• Show prices side-by-side
• Simplify customer decision-making

Examples: Google Hotels, Trivago, Kayak

flashcards.question: Are communication channels part of the distribution system?
flashcards.answer:
NO! Communication channels are NOT part of the distribution system.

They include:
• Media and social media
• Blogs and forums
• Email and telephone

They are:
• Marketing tools
• Promotional channels

When primary suppliers use them directly = direct sales

flashcards.question: What are Switch companies?
flashcards.answer:
Switch companies provide the ELECTRONIC LINK between systems:

• Created when a need surfaced to connect all the disparate CRS systems with the GDS
• They sit between supplier-side software and global distribution

They belong to the supplier-side software companies (with PMS/CRS, booking engine, channel manager).
flashcards.explanation: The 'translators' between hotel systems and the GDS.

flashcards.question: How does the online environment change the tourism business?
flashcards.answer:
Key principle from the lecture:

"The online environment DOES NOT change the business itself, but only the way it is done."

Context:
• Tourism generates up to 10% of the world's GDP (often more in small nations)
• The industry is globalized, with multinational and global companies
• OTAs do the same job as traditional travel agents — only the environment differs
flashcards.explanation: Same business, different way of doing it — a favourite exam quote.

A Channel Manager's main function is to:
options: Synchronize rates and availability across channels

learn.title: Tourism Distribution Chain
learn.content:
The Distribution System

Primary Suppliers → Intermediaries → Digital Platforms → Customer

Tour Operator vs Travel Agent

Key Difference

Tour Operator: CREATES products (packages)

Travel Agent: SELLS products (earns commission)

Key Systems

  • GDS: Global network connecting suppliers with agencies
  • PMS: Internal hotel management system
  • Channel Manager: Syncs availability across channels
  • Meta-Search: Compares prices (Trivago, Kayak)

Exam Alert!

Communication channels (social media, email) are NOT part of the distribution system - they are marketing tools!

flashcards.question: What are the key benefits of the Internet for businesses?
flashcards.answer:
• Faster and cheaper communication
• Easy access to information
• Cost reduction in operations
• Higher efficiency and productivity
• Discovery of new business opportunities
• Closer relationships with customers and suppliers

flashcards.question: How did the Web revolutionize business activities?
flashcards.answer:
1. E-COMMERCE - Online buying and selling
2. DIGITAL MARKETING - Measurable, targeted promotion
3. REMOTE WORK - Location-independent employment
4. DATA ANALYTICS - Data-driven decision-making
5. IMPROVED COMMUNICATION - Real-time global interaction

flashcards.question: What is Web 1.0 (The Read-Only Web)?
flashcards.answer:
Characteristics:
• Static pages
• No user interaction
• Content created only by website owners

Users were PASSIVE readers.
flashcards.explanation: The first generation of the web.

flashcards.question: What is Web 2.0 (The Social Web)?
flashcards.answer:
Characteristics:
• User-generated content
• Social media
• Blogs, comments, tagging

Users became CONTENT CREATORS.

flashcards.question: What is Web 3.0 (The Semantic Web)?
flashcards.answer:
Characteristics:
• Machine-readable data
• Artificial intelligence and machine learning
• Internet of Things
• 3D graphics and virtual environments

The web starts to UNDERSTAND users.

flashcards.question: What is Web 4.0 (The Symbiotic Web)?
flashcards.answer:
Characteristics:
• Human-machine interaction
• Advanced personalization
• AI-driven experiences

Still under development, no fixed definition.

flashcards.question: What is Web 5.0?
flashcards.answer:
Web 5.0 = the (hypothetical) EMOTIONAL web:

• Emotional understanding and empathetic interactions
• Powered by Emotional AI
• Accelerated future: VR, AI, blockchain and more

Evolution summary: 1.0 read-only → 2.0 read-write/social → 3.0 machine-readable/semantic → 4.0 physical-digital fusion (IoT, AI) → 5.0 emotional understanding.
flashcards.explanation: The last column of the Web 1.0–5.0 comparison table from the lecture.

flashcards.question: What is HTTP?
flashcards.answer:
HTTP = HyperText Transfer Protocol

Rules that computers use to communicate over the Internet for web pages.

flashcards.question: What is DNS (Domain Name System)?
flashcards.answer:
DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.

Example:
• You type: google.com
• DNS translates to: 142.250.190.78
• Your browser connects to that IP

flashcards.question: What is the difference between .com and .edu domains?
flashcards.answer:
.com = Commercial organizations
.edu = Educational institutions

Other examples:
.org = Non-profit organizations
.gov = Government
.net = Network providers

flashcards.question: What is the Merchant Model in tourism distribution?
flashcards.answer:
In the Merchant Model:

• Suppliers negotiate NET RATES with intermediaries
• Contracts include blocked rooms (allotment)
• Intermediaries apply a MARK-UP (margin)
• Clients pay the INTERMEDIARY, not supplier
• Client receives a VOUCHER (no price shown)
flashcards.explanation: Tour operators typically use this model.

flashcards.question: What are the advantages of Merchant Model for SUPPLIERS?
flashcards.answer:
Advantages:
• Guaranteed room occupancy in advance
• Predictable net revenues
• Easier price list planning

Disadvantages:
• Lower bargaining power
• Lower revenues (net rates)
• Difficult rate parity control
• Delayed payments (after guest departure)

flashcards.question: What is the Agent Model in tourism distribution?
flashcards.answer:
In the Agent Model:

• Suppliers set the FINAL selling price
• Agents sell at the supplier's price
• Suppliers pay COMMISSION to the agent
• Commission is usually a percentage
• Client gets booking confirmation WITH full price

flashcards.question: What are advantages of Agent Model for SUPPLIERS?
flashcards.answer:
Advantages:
• Higher revenues
• Control over pricing
• Easier rate parity management
• Diversified intermediary network

Disadvantages:
• Complex management of many intermediaries

flashcards.question: What is a Voucher?
flashcards.answer:
A voucher is a document that:

• Confirms prepaid services
• Does NOT show the price
• Is used in the Merchant Model
• Guest presents it at the hotel
flashcards.explanation: Proof of prepayment without price disclosure.

flashcards.question: How does AI support the Merchant Model?
flashcards.answer:
AI in Merchant Model:

• Demand and inventory forecasting
• Automated contract analysis (NLP)
• Dynamic pricing and margin optimization
• Intelligent dynamic packaging

AI predicts demand months ahead and adjusts automatically.
flashcards.explanation: AI enhances but doesn't replace the model.

flashcards.question: How does AI support the Agent Model?
flashcards.answer:
AI in Agent Model (used by OTAs):

• Personalized recommendation systems
• Sentiment analysis of reviews
• AI chatbots and virtual assistants
• Predictive analytics for commission optimization

AI improves conversion rates.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Intermediaries and Infomediaries?
flashcards.answer:
INTERMEDIARIES:
• Participate directly in distribution
• Influence pricing and payments
• Handle transactions

INFOMEDIARIES:
• Provide information only
• Do NOT handle payments
• Support decision-making
• Example: Review sites, comparison sites

flashcards.question: When is the Merchant Model typically used?
flashcards.answer:
Merchant model is typically used by:

• Tour operators
• B2B platforms
• Package trip organizers

Agent model is typically used by:
• Online Travel Agencies (OTAs)
• Booking.com, Expedia

Note: some OTAs (e.g. Expedia) act as merchant OR agent, depending on whether the client prefers to pay in advance.
flashcards.explanation: Different models for different business types.

flashcards.question: Cash flow example: a client books through a TOUR OPERATOR. Hotel net rate = 50, TO sells at 80. Who pays whom?
flashcards.answer:
Flow of money and documents:

• Client pays 80 to the TOUR OPERATOR and receives a VOUCHER (no price shown)
• Hotel invoices the TO for the net rate: Invoice = 50
• TO pays 50 to the hotel
• TO keeps the MARK-UP: 80 − 50 = 30

The client never pays the hotel directly in the merchant model.
flashcards.explanation: Classic merchant-model cash flow from the lecture (Hotel 50 / TO 80 / margin 30).

flashcards.question: Cash flow example: a client books DIRECTLY or through a TRAVEL AGENT. How does the money move?
flashcards.answer:
DIRECT booking:
• Client pays 100 to the hotel, receives Invoice/Receipt = 100

Through a TRAVEL AGENT (agent model, 10% commission):
• Client pays the full price 100
• Hotel receives the payment and pays the agent commission = 10 (agent invoices the hotel for 10)
• Hotel keeps 90

The agent never owns the product — it earns only the commission.
flashcards.explanation: Direct sale vs agent-model cash flow (100 / commission 10 / hotel nets 90).

learn.title: Cash Flows & Business Models
learn.content:
Two Core Distribution Models

MERCHANT MODEL
Supplier → Net Rate → Intermediary adds Mark-up → Client pays Intermediary
Client gets: VOUCHER (no price shown)
AGENT MODEL
Supplier sets Final Price → Agent sells at that price → Earns Commission
Client gets: Booking confirmation (price visible)

Who Uses What?

Merchant: Tour operators, B2B platforms

Agent: OTAs (Booking.com, Expedia)

Intermediaries vs Infomediaries

  • Intermediaries: Handle transactions, influence pricing
  • Infomediaries: Provide info only (reviews, comparisons)

flashcards.question: What is Visual Thinking?
flashcards.answer:
Visual thinking means thinking with images and visualizations.

People process information through two channels:
• Verbal
• Visual

Examples: Road signs, charts, icons, infographics

Text + Image works better than text alone.

flashcards.question: What is Computer Graphics and what are its 3 most common classifications?
flashcards.answer:
GRAPHICS = representation of information with images, where the basic carriers are shapes and colors.

COMPUTER GRAPHICS = graphics where a computer is used to generate, store, process and present image content.

Three most common classifications:
1. INTERACTIVE vs NON-INTERACTIVE (user actively modifies the image vs static display)
2. VECTOR vs RASTER graphics
3. 2D vs 3D graphics
flashcards.explanation: The definition + classification framework of Unit 6.

flashcards.question: What are the 7 Elements of Graphic Design?
flashcards.answer:
The core elements are:

1. LINE - Direction and connection
2. COLOR - Emotions and importance
3. SHAPE - Two-dimensional form
4. TEXTURE - Surface quality
5. SPACE - Positive and negative areas
6. VALUE - Lightness or darkness
7. FORM - 3D appearance

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Warm and Cold Colors?
flashcards.answer:
WARM COLORS:
• Red, orange, yellow, pink, brown
• Energy, warmth, movement
• Dominate and attract attention

COLD COLORS:
• Green, blue, some purples
• Calming and stable
• Suitable for backgrounds

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Vector and Raster Graphics?
flashcards.answer:
VECTOR GRAPHICS:
• Based on mathematical formulas
• Scalable without quality loss
• Small file size
• Not suitable for detailed photos

RASTER GRAPHICS:
• Based on pixels
• Realistic color transitions
• Large file size
• Quality loss when resized
flashcards.explanation: Two fundamental types of digital images.

flashcards.question: What is Resolution?
flashcards.answer:
Resolution describes image clarity/sharpness.

Measured as:
• Pixels (for screens)
• DPI - Dots Per Inch (for print)

Typical values:
• 72-75 DPI - digital display
• 300 DPI - print

Higher resolution = higher detail

flashcards.question: What is the difference between RGB and CMYK color models?
flashcards.answer:
RGB:
• Red, Green, Blue
• Used for SCREENS and digital displays
• Additive color model

CMYK:
• Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black
• Used for PRINTING
• Subtractive color model

flashcards.question: What is the minimum color contrast ratio for accessibility?
flashcards.answer:
Accessibility guidelines:

• Normal text: minimum 4.5:1 contrast ratio
• Large or bold text: minimum 3:1 contrast ratio

This ensures text is readable for people with visual impairments.

flashcards.question: What is the difference between 2D and 3D Graphics?
flashcards.answer:
2D GRAPHICS:
• Flat images
• Simulate depth using color and shadow

3D GRAPHICS:
• Store full spatial information
• Objects can be viewed from any angle
• Use the concept of 'world' or 'space'

flashcards.question: What is Positive and Negative Space?
flashcards.answer:
POSITIVE SPACE:
• Area occupied by objects
• The main subject

NEGATIVE SPACE:
• Empty area around or between objects
• White space

Good use of space improves readability and focus.

flashcards.question: What is the Platform Economy?
flashcards.answer:
The platform economy refers to economic activities enabled by digital platforms that:

• Connect different groups of users
• Facilitate interactions and transactions
• Operate through digital technologies and algorithms

It includes: Sharing economy, Gig economy, Creative economy
flashcards.explanation: The dominant form of digital business.

flashcards.question: What are the key features of Digital Platforms?
flashcards.answer:
Platforms typically:

• Eliminate traditional gatekeepers
• Bring together suppliers and consumers
• Provide infrastructure for transactions
• Govern value creation (don't produce it)
• Operate as complex ecosystems
• Use algorithms and data processing

flashcards.question: How do platforms create value?
flashcards.answer:
Platform value creation is INDIRECT:

• Facilitate interactions
• Enable transactions
• Act mainly as third parties

Value emerges from:
• Gathering many users in one digital space
• Enabling new forms of consumer behavior
• Reconfiguring how value is exchanged

flashcards.question: What are Network Effects?
flashcards.answer:
Network Effects mean:

Each new user increases the value of the platform for existing users.

More users → More connections → More value → Even more users

This explains rapid platform growth.

flashcards.question: What economic concept underlies the positive network effect?
flashcards.answer:
DEMAND-SIDE ECONOMIES OF SCALE (Parker et al., 2016):

• Additional value comes from the DEMAND side (more consumers), not from production costs
• Multiple consumers gathered at one virtual place provide large scalability
• This enables faster interactions and transactions aimed at value creation and exchange
flashcards.explanation: The formal term behind the 'positive network effect'.

flashcards.question: What are examples of platforms in different industries?
flashcards.answer:
Platform examples:

• Retail/Marketplaces: Amazon, Alibaba, eBay
• Accommodation: Airbnb
• Transportation: Uber, BlaBlaCar
• OTAs: Booking.com, Expedia
• Education: Coursera, edX
• Media: YouTube, Netflix
• Freelancing: Fiverr, TaskRabbit

flashcards.question: How does AI transform tourism platforms?
flashcards.answer:
AI in tourism platforms:

• Personalized recommendations based on user data
• Dynamic pricing and revenue optimization
• 24/7 automated customer support (chatbots)

Advanced functions:
• Conversational search
• Automatic translations
• Fraud and fake review detection
• Inventory and rate management

flashcards.question: What are the challenges of the Platform Economy?
flashcards.answer:
Current challenges:

• Unclear and evolving definitions
• Complex role switching between users
• Ethical, social, and environmental impacts
• Regulation and market dominance issues

Future research focuses on:
• Access-based vs asset-controlled models
• Platform governance
• Sustainability of ecosystems

quiz.question: Network effects mean:
options: Each new user increases value for all users

flashcards.question: What is Visual Design vs Graphic Design?
flashcards.answer:
VISUAL DESIGN:
• Problem solvers
• Build and maintain brand's design strategy
• Ensure consistent brand voice across platforms

GRAPHIC DESIGN:
• Focus on conveying specific messages
• Work on individual projects
• Print and digital visuals

Key difference: Visual = brand consistency, Graphic = individual messages

flashcards.question: What is Visual Identity?
flashcards.answer:
Visual identity is everything that visually represents a brand:

• Logo
• Color palette
• Typography
• Images
• Symbols, shapes, patterns

Purpose: Make company recognizable and create emotional impressions.
flashcards.explanation: The visual face of a brand.

flashcards.question: What are the Elements of Visual Identity?
flashcards.answer:
Elements include:

• Brand logo
• Brand color palette (usually max 3 colors)
• Brand fonts and typography
• Brand images and photography style
• Shapes, patterns, textures
• Brand book (style guide)

flashcards.question: What is the difference between Brand, Identity, and Logo?
flashcards.answer:
BRAND:
• How people PERCEIVE the company
• Emotional connection

IDENTITY:
• Visual GUIDELINES supporting the brand
• Design system

LOGO:
• Visual MARK identifying the company
• Most recognizable element

Logo ⊂ Identity ⊂ Brand

flashcards.question: What are the color roles in a brand palette?
flashcards.answer:
Usually no more than 3 main colors:

• PRIMARY color - Main brand color
• SECONDARY color - Background support
• ACCENT color - Emphasis and highlights

Color affects perception and behavior.
flashcards.explanation: Strategic use of color in branding.

flashcards.question: What is a Brand Book (Book of Standards)?
flashcards.answer:
A Brand Book defines rules for visual presentation:

• Logo usage and variants
• Color palettes
• Typography rules
• Icons, illustrations, patterns
• Applications across media

Ensures consistency across all brand touchpoints.

flashcards.question: Why do Infographics work?
flashcards.answer:
Infographics work because:

• Humans learn visually
• Images improve memory and recall
• Brain processes visual and verbal info together

Combines: Text + Images + Data visualization

flashcards.question: What is the VARK learning model?
flashcards.answer:
VARK identifies learning preferences:

• V = Visual - Learning through images and diagrams
• A = Auditory - Learning through listening
• R = Reading/Writing - Learning through text
• K = Kinesthetic - Learning by doing

flashcards.question: What are examples of hidden meanings in logos?
flashcards.answer:
Famous logo hidden meanings:

• Amazon - Arrow from A to Z + smile
• FedEx - Hidden arrow symbolizing speed
• BMW - Colors from Bavarian flag
• Toblerone - Hidden bear in the mountain

flashcards.question: What is the difference between a logomark and a combination logo?
flashcards.answer:
LOGOMARK (logo symbol):
• A symbol alone, without text

COMBINATION LOGO:
• Logo symbol PLUS logotype (text)

TYPOGRAPHIC LOGO:
• No symbol at all — consists only of letters (existing fonts or unique hand-drawn letters)

A logo usually also has sub-variants (black, inverse, horizontal/vertical composition) — all considered ONE logo.

quiz.question: The hierarchy is: Logo is part of Identity, Identity is part of:
Amazon's logo features:
options: An arrow from A to Z and a smile

fillBlanks.sentence: Visual _______ is everything that visually represents a brand.
A Brand _______ defines rules for visual presentation.
Logo ⊂ Identity ⊂ _______.

learn.title: Visual Design & Identity
learn.content:
Visual Design vs Graphic Design

Visual Design: Brand consistency across platforms
Graphic Design: Individual project messages

Visual Identity Elements

  • Logo
  • Color palette (max 3 colors)
  • Typography
  • Images and photography style
  • Patterns and shapes
  • Brand Book (style guide)

Brand Hierarchy

Logo ⊂ Identity ⊂ Brand

Logo is part of Identity, Identity is part of Brand

VARK Learning Model

👁️ Visual - Images, diagrams

👂 Auditory - Listening

📖 Reading/Writing - Text

✋ Kinesthetic - Doing

flashcards.question: What is Digital Marketing?
flashcards.answer:
Digital marketing refers to all marketing activities that use:

• Digital channels
• Digital devices
• Online platforms

It combines: Advertising + Sales + Data Analytics

Goal: Attract customers, influence buying decisions, increase market share.

flashcards.question: What are the core benefits of Digital Marketing?
flashcards.answer:
Key benefits:

1. WIDE REACH - Global audiences, no geographical barriers
2. COST EFFICIENCY - Social media and blogs are inexpensive
3. MEASURABLE RESULTS - Analytics track everything
4. PERSONALIZATION - Segment audiences, personalize messages
5. ENGAGEMENT - Interact before, during, and after purchase
6. EASY CONVERSIONS - Few clicks from ad to purchase

flashcards.question: What is SEO (Search Engine Optimization)?
flashcards.answer:
SEO improves website visibility in ORGANIC (unpaid) search results.

Key SEO areas:
• ON-PAGE SEO - Content and keywords
• OFF-PAGE SEO - Backlinks and authority
• TECHNICAL SEO - Speed, structure, performance

flashcards.question: What is SEM (Search Engine Marketing)?
flashcards.answer:
SEM uses PAID ads in search engine results.

• Advertisers pay per click (PPC)
• Ads appear for specific keywords
• Immediate visibility

SEO + PPC = SEM

flashcards.question: What is Content Marketing?
flashcards.answer:
Content Marketing includes:

• Blogs
• Ebooks
• Newsletters
• Infographics
• Podcasts
• Videos

Goal: Provide valuable content to attract and retain customers.

flashcards.question: What is Affiliate Marketing?
flashcards.answer:
Affiliate Marketing:

• Uses third parties to promote products
• Pays commission only AFTER a sale
• Performance-based model

Example: Bloggers earning commission for product recommendations.

flashcards.question: What is Marketing Automation?
flashcards.answer:
Marketing Automation uses:

• AI and machine learning
• Automated workflows

It helps with:
• Campaign management
• Performance measurement
• ROI calculation
• Personalized messaging at scale

flashcards.question: What makes video marketing effective?
flashcards.answer:
Video Marketing:

• Communicates more in less time
• Increases engagement
• Highly shareable

Platforms:
• YouTube (also a search engine!)
• TikTok
• Instagram

Video is the most consumed content format.

flashcards.question: What is Influencer Marketing?
flashcards.answer:
Influencer Marketing:

• Uses trusted content creators
• Leverages established audiences
• Authentic and relatable

Influencers have built trust with their followers, making recommendations more effective.

Difference vs affiliate: the influencer is paid a FLAT FEE regardless of sales; an affiliate earns only per sale.

flashcards.question: What are ALL 11 types of digital marketing from the lecture?
flashcards.answer:
1. Content marketing (blogs, ebooks, podcasts…)
2. SEO
3. SEM (paid search: Google Ads, Bing Ads)
4. Social media marketing
5. PPC (pay per click)
6. Affiliate marketing
7. Marketing automation (AI/ML)
8. Email marketing
9. Mobile/SMS marketing
10. Video marketing
11. Influencer marketing
flashcards.explanation: The full list — exam questions often ask you to name several.

flashcards.question: What are Email marketing and Mobile (SMS) marketing?
flashcards.answer:
EMAIL MARKETING — direct marketing via strategic emails:
• Newsletters, welcome emails, holiday promotions, post-purchase follow-ups
• Still the quickest, most direct way to reach customers

MOBILE/SMS MARKETING — tailored to mobile devices and wearables:
• Timely one-on-one SMS messages (phones are with us 24/7)
• Companies report ~102% ROI on SMS marketing

flashcards.question: What do famous digital campaigns (Nike, Heineken, Airbnb) teach us?
flashcards.answer:
NIKE — #JustDoIt (since 1987): a forceful, commanding slogan can define a brand globally (viral marketing).

HEINEKEN — "Cheers to All": reverse gender expectations, keep it lighthearted, create global (image-based) content, upload natively to each platform.

AIRBNB — "Made Possible by Hosts": video-first, mute-friendly, real people via UGC (user-generated content), sentimental storytelling.

quiz.question: Which is NOT a content marketing format?
On-page SEO involves:
options: Content and keywords on your site

quiz.question: Companies report approximately what ROI on SMS marketing?
Unlike affiliates, influencers are typically paid:
options: A flat fee regardless of sales

learn.title: Digital Marketing
learn.content:
Core Benefits of Digital Marketing

  • 🌍 Wide Reach: Global audiences
  • 💰 Cost Efficiency: Lower costs than traditional
  • 📊 Measurable: Track everything with analytics
  • 👤 Personalization: Target specific audiences
  • 🔄 Engagement: Interact at every stage

SEO vs SEM

SEO = Organic search optimization (FREE clicks)
SEM = SEO + PPC (PAID clicks)
PPC = Pay Per Click advertising

Types of Digital Marketing

  • Content Marketing (blogs, videos)
  • Social Media Marketing
  • Email Marketing
  • Affiliate Marketing (commission-based)
  • Influencer Marketing
  • Video Marketing (YouTube, TikTok)

flashcards.question: What is Social Media?
flashcards.answer:
Social media refers to digital technologies that enable users to:

• Create content
• Share information
• Interact and communicate with others

Platforms: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X (Twitter), LinkedIn

flashcards.question: What are the key social media statistics?
flashcards.answer:
Global insights:

• Over 5.41 billion active users worldwide
• Average daily usage: ~143 minutes
• ~98% of users access via mobile devices

flashcards.question: Why is Social Media important for business?
flashcards.answer:
Business benefits:

• Raise brand awareness
• Discover and research customers
• Communicate directly with audiences
• Support sales and conversions
• Build community and loyalty

flashcards.question: What are the characteristics of Facebook?
flashcards.answer:
Facebook:

• Over 3 billion monthly active users
• Strong advertising ecosystem
• Dominant in brand discovery and communities

Effective for:
• Broad audiences
• Advertising campaigns
• Brand pages and groups

flashcards.question: What are the characteristics of TikTok?
flashcards.answer:
TikTok:

• Extremely high engagement
• Short-form video content
• Strong influence on younger generations
• Highest average time spent per user
• Over 90% of users interact after watching

Powerful for:
• Viral marketing
• Storytelling through video
• Trend-driven campaigns
flashcards.explanation: The rising star of social media.

flashcards.question: What are the characteristics of YouTube?
flashcards.answer:
YouTube:

• A social media platform AND second-largest search engine
• Billions of active users
• Strong purchase influence

Ideal for:
• Long-form content
• Tutorials and reviews
• Brand storytelling

flashcards.question: What are the characteristics of LinkedIn?
flashcards.answer:
LinkedIn:

• Leading professional platform
• Strong B2B focus
• High-quality content distribution
• Effective lead generation

Best for:
• Employer branding
• Professional visibility
• B2B marketing

flashcards.question: Which platforms do different generations prefer?
flashcards.answer:
Generational preferences:

• Gen Z: TikTok, Instagram, Snapchat
• Millennials: Instagram, Facebook, YouTube
• Gen X: Facebook, YouTube
• Baby Boomers: Facebook, messaging apps

flashcards.question: What makes social media content go viral?
flashcards.answer:
Viral content characteristics:

• Emotional impact
• Simplicity
• Relatability
• Strong visual elements

Content that triggers emotions spreads faster.

flashcards.question: What are social media future trends?
flashcards.answer:
Key future directions:

• Short-form video dominance
• Growth of social commerce
• AI-driven personalization
• Immersive AR and VR experiences
• Stronger focus on authenticity and privacy

flashcards.question: What is Google Analytics?
flashcards.answer:
Google Analytics (GA) is a web analytics tool providing insights into:

• Website performance
• User behavior
• Traffic sources
• Conversions and goals

Supports: Digital marketing, SEO, PPC, content optimization, e-commerce

flashcards.question: How does Google Analytics work?
flashcards.answer:
GA works by:

1. Adding a JavaScript tracking code to website pages
2. Collecting user interaction data when pages load
3. Sending data to Google servers
4. Displaying results in reports and dashboards

flashcards.question: What Real-Time data does GA provide?
flashcards.answer:
Real-Time data shows:

• Active users on the website right now
• Pages being viewed at the moment
• Device type (desktop or mobile)
• User locations

Useful for monitoring live campaigns.

flashcards.question: What Audience Insights does GA provide?
flashcards.answer:
Audience insights include:

• Number of visitors and sessions
• New vs returning users
• Session duration
• Pages per session
• Demographics and interests

flashcards.question: What is Goal and Conversion Tracking in GA?
flashcards.answer:
Goals represent desired user actions:

• Purchases
• Form submissions
• Newsletter sign-ups
• Downloads
• Account creation

Conversions measure how many users complete these goals.

flashcards.question: What are the 5 key benefits of Google Analytics?
flashcards.answer:
1. ACCESS TO REAL-TIME DATA — live users, pageviews, top pages and locations
2. INSIGHTS INTO YOUR AUDIENCE — visitors, sessions, new vs returning, interests
3. ENHANCED AD MANAGEMENT — track Google Ads clicks, cost per click, campaign costs in one place
4. UNDERSTANDING USER BEHAVIOR — most popular content, bounce rate, what drives conversions
5. BETTER TRACKING OF GOALS & CONVERSIONS — what is completed, where, and its value

flashcards.question: What is Google Trends?
flashcards.answer:
Google Trends is a FREE tool that analyzes the popularity of search terms.

It:
• Measures RELATIVE popularity, not absolute volume
• Compares search interest across time and regions
• Normalizes data for fair comparison

flashcards.question: What are practical uses of Google Trends?
flashcards.answer:
Practical uses:

• Identify trending topics
• Detect seasonal demand patterns
• Support local SEO strategies
• Analyze competitors
• Optimize keyword strategies
• Understand market interest

flashcards.question: Google Analytics vs Google Trends - What's the difference?
flashcards.answer:
GOOGLE ANALYTICS:
• Focuses on YOUR website
• Behavior and conversions
• Performance metrics

GOOGLE TRENDS:
• Focuses on OVERALL market interest
• External search behavior
• Popularity comparisons

quiz.question: GA works by adding what to website pages?
GA Real-Time data shows:
options: Active users and pages viewed right now

quiz.question: Goals in GA represent:
options: Desired user actions like purchases or sign-ups

quiz.question: Google Trends is useful for:
options: Identifying trending topics and seasonal patterns

quiz.question: GA Audience Insights include:
options: New vs returning users, session duration, demographics

learn.title: Google Analytics & Trends
learn.content:

Tracking Code → Collects Data → Reports & Dashboards

Key GA Features

  • 📊 Real-Time: Active users now
  • 👥 Audience: Who visits your site
  • 📈 Behavior: What they do on site
  • 🎯 Conversions: Goal completions

Google Trends

Uses

  • Identify trending topics
  • Detect seasonal patterns
  • Compare keyword popularity
  • Analyze competitors

Key Difference

GA: YOUR website performance

Trends: MARKET search interest

flashcards.question: What is SERP?
flashcards.answer:
SERP = Search Engine Results Page

The page displayed after a user enters a query into a search engine.

Contains:
• Organic results (SEO)
• Paid ads (PPC)
• Featured snippets
• Local results

flashcards.question: What is SEO?
flashcards.answer:
SEO = Search Engine Optimization

Focuses on optimizing a website to:
• Rank higher in ORGANIC search results
• Attract UNPAID traffic

FOUR main subcategories:
• On-page SEO
• Off-page SEO
• Technical SEO
• User Interaction Signals

Google uses 200+ ranking signals in its algorithm.
flashcards.explanation: Getting free search traffic — note: FOUR subcategories, not three.

flashcards.question: What are User Interaction Signals in SEO?
flashcards.answer:
The 4th SEO subcategory — how users interact with your site tells Google whether your page matches the search:

• High BOUNCE RATE → page may not answer the query → rankings can drop
• CTR (click-through rate) → better titles/descriptions raise it
• DWELL TIME → how long a visitor stays; longer = more relevant content
flashcards.explanation: Same signals reappear as ranking factor #10 (on-page experience).

flashcards.question: What is SEM?
flashcards.answer:
SEM = Search Engine Marketing

A broader concept that includes:
• SEO (organic)
• PPC (paid advertising)

SEO + PPC = SEM

Aims to maximize visibility on search engines.

flashcards.question: What is Quality Score in Google Ads?
flashcards.answer:
Quality Score measures how relevant and useful an ad is.

Based on:
• Expected click-through rate
• Ad relevance to search query
• Landing page experience

Higher Quality Score = Lower costs, better positions.

flashcards.question: SEO vs SEM - Speed difference?
flashcards.answer:
SPEED:

SEO:
• Slow to show results
• On average it takes ~2 YEARS to rank on the first page of Google (many top pages are 3+ years old)
• Long-tail keywords + best practices can bring first results within a few months

SEM (PPC):
• Immediate visibility — run an ad in the morning, get traffic in the afternoon
• But positive ROI can still take months of testing and tweaking

flashcards.question: Is SEO really 'free traffic'?
flashcards.answer:
NO — you don't pay per click, but SEO is NOT free:

• Quality, unique content costs many hours of labour
• Building domain authority requires consistent top content + promotion
• SEO tools (ahrefs, semrush…) can cost ~$350/month
• You pay website designers and developers
• It requires a broad knowledge base built over years
flashcards.explanation: The 'SEO costs' reality check from the lecture.

flashcards.question: What is High-Quality Content in SEO?
flashcards.answer:
Content quality is the STRONGEST ranking factor.

Quality content is:
• Unique
• Fresh
• Useful
• Written for USERS, not search engines

Google rewards valuable content.

flashcards.question: What are Backlinks in SEO?
flashcards.answer:
Backlinks are links from other websites to your site.

They act as:
• Votes of confidence
• Authority signals

More quality backlinks = Higher rankings.

Part of OFF-PAGE SEO.

flashcards.question: What is Mobile-First Indexing?
flashcards.answer:
Google uses MOBILE-FIRST indexing.

This means:
• Mobile version is used for ranking
• Responsive design is essential
• Desktop-only sites may rank lower

Most users browse on mobile!

flashcards.question: What are Core Web Vitals?
flashcards.answer:
Core Web Vitals measure:

• Loading speed (LCP)
• Interactivity (FID)
• Visual stability (CLS)

Part of Google's ranking factors.
Fast websites rank better!

flashcards.question: What are the 10 most important Google ranking factors?
flashcards.answer:
Top ranking factors:

1. High-quality content
2. Backlinks
3. Search intent & relevance
4. Website loading speed
5. Mobile friendliness
6. Domain authority
7. Keyword optimization
8. Website structure
9. Website security (HTTPS)
10. User experience signals (CTR, bounce rate)

quiz.question: Backlinks are:
options: Links on your site to yourself
Links from other websites to your site

quiz.question: Mobile-first indexing means:
options: Mobile version is used for ranking

learn.title: SEO, SEM & SERP
learn.content:
Key Definitions

SERP = Search Engine Results Page
SEO = Search Engine Optimization (organic)
SEM = SEO + PPC (all search marketing)

SEO Types

  • On-Page: Content, keywords, meta tags
  • Off-Page: Backlinks, authority
  • Technical: Speed, structure, mobile

Top Ranking Factors

  1. High-quality content
  2. Backlinks (authority)
  3. Search intent match
  4. Loading speed
  5. Mobile-friendliness

SEO vs PPC Speed

⏳ SEO: Months to years for results

⚡ PPC: Immediate traffic

flashcards.question: What is a Property Management System (PMS)?
flashcards.answer:
A PMS is a software platform that automates a hotel's daily operations.

It supports:
• Daily hotel operations
• Administrative and financial tasks
• Guest experience management

The digital backbone of hotel operations.

flashcards.question: What factors influence PMS adoption?
flashcards.answer:
Factors affecting PMS adoption:

• HOTEL SIZE: <20 rooms often without PMS; 100+ rooms nearly 100% adoption
• OWNERSHIP: Chains/franchises usually have PMS; independents less likely
• STAR RATING: 3+ stars higher adoption; 4-5 stars require PMS
• OCCUPANCY: High occupancy increases need for PMS

flashcards.question: What are the main PMS functionalities?
flashcards.answer:
Main PMS functionalities:

• Reservation systems
• Front-desk operations
• Housekeeping
• Customer data management (CRM)
• Revenue management
• Reports and analytics
• Point of Sale (POS)
• Back-office management

flashcards.question: What are the mandatory PMS modules?
flashcards.answer:
Every PMS MUST include:

1. RESERVATION SYSTEM:
• Stores inventory and availability
• Synchronizes dates and room status
• Integrates with booking engine and channels

2. FRONT-DESK OPERATIONS:
• Manages reservation status
• Check-in and check-out
• Payment processing
• Room status control

flashcards.question: What does the Revenue Management module do?
flashcards.answer:
Revenue Management uses:

• Historical booking data
• Forecasting algorithms

To support:
• Dynamic pricing
• Occupancy optimization
• Revenue maximization

Key KPIs: Occupancy rate, ADR, RevPAR

flashcards.question: What is ADR and RevPAR?
flashcards.answer:
ADR = Average Daily Rate
• Average revenue per occupied room
• Formula: Room Revenue / Rooms Sold

RevPAR = Revenue Per Available Room
• Revenue per ALL rooms (occupied + empty)
• Formula: Room Revenue / Total Rooms Available

Or: ADR × Occupancy Rate

flashcards.question: What does the POS module manage?
flashcards.answer:
POS (Point of Sale) manages transactions beyond accommodation:

• Restaurants and cafés
• Spa and gym services
• In-room services
• Minibar, TV, and Wi-Fi charges

All charges link to guest folio.

flashcards.question: What does the Customer Data Management module do?
flashcards.answer:
Stores ALL guest data to build relationships during and after the stay:

• Integrates with front desk + reservation system (derives guest info from them)
• Should integrate with the hotel's existing CRM, if there is one
• Supports marketing: measures guest experience through the stay and after
• Powers PERSONALIZATION via membership and LOYALTY programs (especially important for chains and resorts)
flashcards.explanation: The CRM side of the PMS.

flashcards.question: What is the future of PMS?
flashcards.answer:
Modern PMS developments:

• Integration with hotel mobile applications
• Remote check-in and digital ID upload
• Mobile communication between guests and staff
• Cloud-based systems
• AI-powered features

quiz.question: Hotels with 100+ rooms have PMS adoption rate of:
POS module manages:
options: Restaurant, spa, and other non-room charges

flashcards.question: Why is security critical in E-Business?
flashcards.answer:
E-business depends on TRUST.

Security is essential for:
• Protecting customer information
• Ensuring safe online transactions
• Maintaining brand reputation
• Complying with legal and industry standards

flashcards.question: What are the 4 fundamental principles of E-Commerce Security?
flashcards.answer:
Four principles:

1. PRIVACY - Data accessed only by authorized parties
2. INTEGRITY - Data remains unchanged during storage/transmission
3. AUTHENTICATION - Both parties are verified as real
4. NON-REPUDIATION - Neither party can deny completed transaction

flashcards.question: What is Privacy in E-Commerce Security?
flashcards.answer:
Privacy ensures customer data is accessed only by authorized parties.

Protection methods:
• Antivirus software
• Firewalls
• Encryption
• Data protection systems

flashcards.question: What is Non-Repudiation?
flashcards.answer:
Non-repudiation means neither the buyer nor seller can DENY a completed transaction.

Achieved through:
• Digital signatures
• Transaction logs
• Certificates

Provides legal proof of transaction.

flashcards.question: What are common E-Commerce cybersecurity risks?
flashcards.answer:
Common risks:

• Data breaches
• Hacking and malware
• Phishing attacks
• SQL injection
• DDoS attacks
• Credit card fraud

flashcards.question: What makes a strong password?
flashcards.answer:
Strong passwords:

• Include numbers and special characters
• Combine uppercase and lowercase letters
• Are unique for each platform
• Are long (12+ characters recommended)
• Avoid personal information

flashcards.question: What are SSL Certificates and HTTPS?
flashcards.answer:
SSL Certificates:
• Encrypt data between user and server
• Convert HTTP into HTTPS
• Show padlock icon in browser

HTTPS = Secure communication
Google confirmed HTTPS as a ranking signal.

flashcards.question: What is PCI-DSS?
flashcards.answer:
PCI-DSS = Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard

Security standard for businesses handling credit card data.

Requires:
• Firewalls
• Strong passwords
• Secure data storage
• Antivirus protection
• Encryption

flashcards.question: What should a secure hosting provider offer?
flashcards.answer:
A secure hosting provider offers:

• Threat monitoring
• Regular security upgrades
• Fast issue resolution
• Built-in security features
• DDoS protection
• Regular backups

flashcards.question: What are the 10 e-commerce security tips to protect a business?
flashcards.answer:
1. Suggest STRONG PASSWORDS (unique per login)
2. Implement MULTILAYER security
3. Use a FIREWALL (blocks DDoS, SQL injection)
4. Use a PAYMENT PROVIDER — never store customer financial data on company servers
5. Install an SSL certificate (HTTPS) — 64% of users leave a site on a 'Not secure' warning
6. UPDATE software and hardware (patches fix vulnerabilities)
7. Follow PCI-DSS requirements
8. BACK UP data routinely
9. Establish best practices — educate employees and customers
10. Choose the right HOSTING provider

quiz.question: The 4 security principles are Privacy, Integrity, Authentication, and:
Non-repudiation means:
options: Neither party can deny a transaction

quiz.question: Strong passwords should:
options: Be the same for all sites
Include numbers, special characters, and be unique

quiz.question: Common cyber risks include all EXCEPT:

learn.title: E-Business Security
learn.content:
4 Security Principles

1. Privacy - Only authorized access
2. Integrity - Data unchanged
3. Authentication - Verify identity
4. Non-repudiation - Cannot deny transaction

Common Threats

  • 🔓 Data breaches
  • 🎣 Phishing attacks
  • 💉 SQL injection
  • 🌊 DDoS attacks
  • 💳 Credit card fraud

Protection Methods

  • SSL/HTTPS encryption

flashcards.question: Which units make up the two midterm 'halves' that the final combines?
flashcards.answer:
1st midterm (Units 1–7): the context of modern e-commerce, tourism distribution chain, internet/www as business platform, relationships & cash flows (merchant/agent models), computer graphics, and platform economy.
2nd midterm (Units 8–15): visual design & identity, digital marketing, social media, Google Analytics & Trends, SEO/SEM/SERP, hotel PMS, e-business security, and challenges & trends.
flashcards.explanation: The course follows the 14 lecture decks; the final covers everything.

flashcards.question: Trace one hotel room from supplier to client through BOTH distribution models.
flashcards.answer:
MERCHANT: hotel gives a NET RATE (e.g. 50) with blocked rooms (allotment) → tour operator adds MARK-UP and sells at 80 → client pays the TO and receives a VOUCHER (no price shown) → hotel invoices the TO for 50; TO keeps 30.
AGENT: hotel sets the FINAL price (e.g. 100) → agent sells at that price → hotel pays the agent a negotiated COMMISSION (e.g. 10) → client gets a booking confirmation WITH the price.
flashcards.explanation: The single most important exam skill from Units 4–5.

flashcards.question: How do the platform economy and the tourism distribution chain connect?
flashcards.answer: OTAs (Booking.com, Expedia — B2C), bedbanks (Hotelbeds — B2B), GDS (Amadeus, Sabre — B2B) and review sites (TripAdvisor — C2C) are all PLATFORMS inside the distribution chain. They eliminate gatekeepers, connect suppliers and consumers, don't produce value themselves but govern value creation, and grow through network effects (demand-side economies of scale).
flashcards.explanation: Units 2 + 7 always pair well in cross-topic questions.

flashcards.question: Connect SEO, SEM, PPC, SERP and Google Analytics into one picture.
flashcards.answer: The SERP shows ORGANIC results (won via SEO: on-page, off-page, technical + user interaction signals) and PAID results (PPC ads, bought via bidding; Quality Score lowers your cost per click). SEM is the umbrella = SEO + PPC. Google Analytics then measures what happens after the click on YOUR site (audience, behavior, conversions), while Google Trends measures overall MARKET search interest.
flashcards.explanation: Units 11 + 12 as one funnel: visibility → click → measurement.

flashcards.question: Which PMS modules are mandatory, and which hotel KPIs do PMS reports track?
flashcards.answer:
Mandatory modules: RESERVATION SYSTEM and FRONT-DESK OPERATIONS (others: customer data/CRM, revenue management, reports & analytics, POS, back-office).
Key KPIs in reports: OCCUPANCY RATE, ADR (room revenue / rooms sold) and RevPAR (room revenue / ALL available rooms = ADR × occupancy).
flashcards.explanation: Unit 13 — the two 'must' modules plus the metric trio.

flashcards.question: Summarise the 4 security principles and the biggest e-business challenges in hospitality.
flashcards.answer:
Security principles (Unit 14): PRIVACY (authorized access only), INTEGRITY (data unchanged), AUTHENTICATION (both parties real), NON-REPUDIATION (no denying transactions — digital signatures).
Challenges (Unit 15): technology implementation costs, legacy system integration, rising customer expectations, mobile optimization, overloading guests with tech / loss of human touch, and data security & GDPR compliance.
flashcards.explanation: The defensive half of the course in one card.

learn.content:

A cross-topic practice set that combines all 15 units — exactly how the final mixes them. Use it AFTER reviewing the two midterm halves.
